meta.title: Parable of the Sower · C1 起步词表
meta.author: Octavia E. Butler

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 适应能力，可调整性
records.usage: adaptability to change 对变化的适应力；adapt 是调整，adaptable 是能适应的。

originals.text: INTELLIGENCE IS ONGOING, INDIVIDUAL adaptability.
originals.zh: 智慧是不断发展的个性化适应能力。

examples.en: The job demands adaptability as well as technical skill.
examples.zh: 这份工作既需要技术，也需要适应能力。

examples.en: The plant's adaptability helps it survive in poor soil.
examples.zh: 这种植物的适应性使它能在贫瘠土壤中存活。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 本质，核心；精华液
records.usage: at its essence 从本质看；in essence 实质上；the essence of ……的精髓。

originals.text: PRODIGY IS, AT ITS essence, adaptability and persistent, positive obsession.
originals.zh: 天才在本质上结合了变通、坚韧和积极的迷恋。

examples.en: Trust is the essence of their partnership.
examples.zh: 信任是他们合作关系的核心。

examples.en: The two proposals are, in essence, identical.
examples.zh: 两项提议实质上完全相同。

examples.en: Add a drop of vanilla essence.
examples.zh: 加入一滴香草精。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 强烈痴迷，执念
records.usage: an obsession with 对……的痴迷；本书 positive obsession 为正向、持续的专注，不必一律贬译。

originals.text: Without positive obsession, there is nothing at all.
originals.zh: 没有积极的迷恋，就什么也不剩。

examples.en: Her obsession with detail improved the final design.
examples.zh: 她对细节的执着改善了最终设计。

examples.en: Winning had become an unhealthy obsession.
examples.zh: 获胜成了一种不健康的执念。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: adj. 持续的；坚持不懈的
records.usage: persistent pain/noise 持续疼痛／噪声；persistent efforts 不懈努力。

originals.text: Not a very subtle image, but a persistent one.
originals.zh: 梦境并不十分晦涩，但是一直持续出现。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 3 段

examples.en: A persistent cough kept him awake.
examples.zh: 持续的咳嗽让他无法入睡。

examples.en: Her persistent questions finally produced an answer.
examples.zh: 她坚持追问，终于得到了答复。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 奇才，神童；非凡的人或事
records.usage: a child prodigy 神童；本书题辞把非凡才能与适应力、执着相联系。

originals.text: PRODIGY IS, AT ITS essence, adaptability and persistent, positive obsession.
originals.zh: 天才在本质上结合了变通、坚韧和积极的迷恋。

examples.en: The pianist was celebrated as a child prodigy.
examples.zh: 这位钢琴家曾被誉为神童。

examples.en: Being a prodigy did not spare her years of practice.
examples.zh: 即使是奇才，她也经历了多年练习。

records.gradeSource: 依据 English Vocabulary Profile 编制的 C2 二手汇编，作词条参考；不是官方穷尽清单。
records.meaning: n. 坚持；持续存在
records.usage: persistence in doing 坚持做；the persistence of a problem 问题持续存在。

originals.text: Without persistence, what remains is an enthusiasm of the moment.
originals.zh: 没有坚韧，就只剩下三分钟热血；

examples.en: Her persistence paid off after several rejections.
examples.zh: 几次被拒后，她的坚持终于有了回报。

examples.en: The persistence of the smell suggested a hidden leak.
examples.zh: 气味一直不散，说明可能有隐蔽的泄漏。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: adj. 破坏性的，毁灭性的
records.usage: destructive behavior 破坏性行为；destructive criticism 打击式批评，与 constructive 建设性的相对。

originals.text: Without adaptability, what remains may be channeled into destructive fanaticism.
originals.zh: 没有变通，也许会陷入毁灭性的疯狂；

examples.en: The storm was unusually destructive.
examples.zh: 这场风暴的破坏力格外大。

examples.en: Their constant rivalry became destructive.
examples.zh: 他们持续的竞争变得有害。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 狂热，盲信
records.usage: religious/political fanaticism 宗教／政治狂热；比 enthusiasm 更暗示极端和不容异见。

originals.text: Without adaptability, what remains may be channeled into destructive fanaticism.
originals.zh: 没有变通，也许会陷入毁灭性的疯狂；

examples.en: The novel examines the cost of political fanaticism.
examples.zh: 小说探讨政治狂热的代价。

examples.en: Her enthusiasm never hardened into fanaticism.
examples.zh: 她的热情从未僵化为盲信。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 反复发生，再现
records.usage: recurring dream 反复做的梦；a recurring problem 反复出现的问题；注意双写 r。

originals.text: I HAD MY RECURRING dream last night.
originals.zh: 不断浮现的梦境昨晚再临。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 2 段

examples.en: The same image recurred in three dreams.
examples.zh: 同一画面在三个梦中反复出现。

examples.en: If the error recurs, record the exact message.
examples.zh: 错误若再次出现，请记下完整提示。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: v./n. 扭转；弯曲；意外转折
records.usage: twist one's ankle 扭伤脚踝；a twist in the plot 情节转折；twist someone's words 歪曲话语。

originals.text: I saw its bloody wounds as it twisted.
originals.zh: 身体扭曲时，我看见它流血的伤口。
originals.location: 第 4 章 · 第 99 段

examples.en: She twisted the lid until it came loose.
examples.zh: 她拧了拧盖子，终于拧松了。

examples.en: The final chapter contains an unexpected twist.
examples.zh: 最后一章有个意外转折。

examples.en: He accused the reporter of twisting his words.
examples.zh: 他指责记者歪曲了他的话。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 提醒物，提醒信息
records.usage: a reminder of 提醒人想起……的事物；send a reminder 发送提醒。

originals.text: What a pity to spoil it with reminders of reality.
originals.zh: 这段美好安逸的休闲时光就要被无情的现实践踏，真是可惜。
originals.location: 第 6 章 · 第 88 段

examples.en: The scar is a reminder of the accident.
examples.zh: 那道疤提醒着她那场事故。

examples.en: I set a reminder to renew my passport.
examples.zh: 我设了提醒去换护照。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 腾空，悬浮；使升空
records.usage: 既可不及物，也可及物；常见魔术、幻想或磁悬浮语境。

originals.text: I’m learning to fly, to levitate myself.
originals.zh: 梦中我学习飞行，浮在空中。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 3 段

examples.en: The magician appeared to levitate above the stage.
examples.zh: 魔术师看起来悬浮在舞台上方。

examples.en: The device uses magnets to levitate a small ball.
examples.zh: 装置利用磁铁让小球悬浮。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: adj. 微妙的，不易察觉的；精巧的
records.usage: a subtle difference 区别细微；subtle humor 含蓄幽默；b 不发音。

originals.text: Not a very subtle image, but a persistent one.
originals.zh: 梦境并不十分晦涩，但是一直持续出现。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 3 段

examples.en: There is a subtle difference between the two translations.
examples.zh: 两种译法之间有细微差别。

examples.en: The sauce has a subtle taste of lemon.
examples.zh: 酱汁有淡淡的柠檬味。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 抓紧，握住；理解，领会；n. 掌握，理解力
records.usage: grasp someone's wrist 抓住手腕；grasp an idea 领会概念；have a good grasp of 熟练掌握；beyond one's grasp 难以理解或够不着。

originals.text: Holding my body stiff and tense, I let go of whatever I’m grasping, whatever has kept me from rising or falling so far.
originals.zh: 紧绷着僵硬的身体，我放开抓握的手，在此之前我没能升起或坠落正是因为有它。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 4 段

originals.text: He grasped my wrist, seemed ready to push it away.
originals.zh: 他抓住我的手腕，似乎准备推开，然后他抓得更紧，不让它移走，“你就要离开这里，留下我一个人。”
originals.location: 第 13 章 · 第 30 段

examples.en: She grasped the rope with both hands.
examples.zh: 她双手抓紧绳子。

examples.en: It took me a while to grasp the distinction.
examples.zh: 我花了一会儿才理解那个区别。

examples.en: The prize was finally within his grasp.
examples.zh: 奖项终于触手可及了。

examples.en: She tightened her grasp on the rope.
examples.zh: 她把绳子抓得更紧了。

examples.en: She grasped the rail as the boat rocked.
examples.zh: 船摇晃时，她抓住了栏杆。

records.gradeSource: 依据 English Vocabulary Profile 编制的 C2 二手汇编，作词条参考；不是官方穷尽清单。
records.meaning: adj. 僵硬的；紧张拘谨的；强烈的
records.usage: stiff with anger 气得僵住；stiff competition 激烈竞争；stiff muscles 僵硬肌肉。

originals.text: Allie swung around, stiff with anger.
originals.zh: 艾莉急转回身，因为怒火而僵住。
originals.location: 第 19 章 · 第 124 段

examples.en: My shoulders were stiff after the long drive.
examples.zh: 长途驾驶后，我的肩膀僵硬了。

examples.en: The proposal faces stiff opposition.
examples.zh: 提案面临强烈反对。

examples.en: Their first conversation was rather stiff.
examples.zh: 他们第一次交谈颇为拘谨。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: adj. 紧绷的，紧张的；v. 绷紧；n. 时态
records.usage: go tense 绷紧；a tense atmosphere 紧张气氛；past tense 过去时。

originals.text: I could see them straighten and go tense as I approached.
originals.zh: 我起身走向那对情侣，接近他们时，我能看见他们挺直了身体，变得紧张。
originals.location: 第 17 章 · 第 117 段

examples.en: His arms tensed when the door opened.
examples.zh: 门开时，他的手臂绷紧了。

examples.en: The room remained tense throughout the meeting.
examples.zh: 会议期间，屋里一直气氛紧张。

examples.en: This sentence shifts unexpectedly into the present tense.
examples.zh: 这句话突然转用了现在时。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: v. 绷紧，用力；n. 压力，负担；品系
records.usage: strain upward 用力向上；strain a muscle 拉伤肌肉；under strain 承压；科学语境还可指应变。

originals.text: And I lean into the air, straining upward, not moving upward, but not quite falling down either.
originals.zh: 我探出身体，向上用力，虽然没有升高，但是也没有下落，然后我真的开始移动，仿佛飘在离地一两米的空中滑行，心里同时充满恐惧和欣喜。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 4 段

examples.en: The experiment measured strain in the glass as it cooled.
examples.zh: 实验测量了玻璃冷却时的应变。

examples.en: The extra workload put a strain on their relationship.
examples.zh: 额外工作量给他们的关系造成了压力。

examples.en: She strained her shoulder lifting the box.
examples.zh: 她抬箱子时拉伤了肩膀。

examples.en: She strained to hear the voice through the wall.
examples.zh: 她竭力听清隔墙传来的声音。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: v./n. 飘移；逐渐偏离；大意
records.usage: drift through the room 在房间里飘过；drift off 睡着；get the drift 明白大意。常暗示缺少主动控制。

originals.text: Natividad fed Dominic and the two of them drifted off to sleep.
originals.zh: 纳蒂维达给多米尼克喂奶时两人双双入睡，艾莉照着之前的样子与贾斯汀相处，不过给他准备饮食有点复杂。
originals.location: 第 21 章 · 第 8 段

examples.en: Leaves drifted across the pond.
examples.zh: 树叶漂过池塘。

examples.en: The discussion drifted away from the original question.
examples.zh: 讨论渐渐偏离了原来的问题。

examples.en: I missed a few words, but I got the drift.
examples.zh: 我漏听了几个词，不过懂了大意。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 熊熊燃烧，闪耀；n. 大火，强光
records.usage: blaze up 燃起；a blaze of light 一片灿烂光芒；blaze a trail 开辟道路。

originals.text: It blazes up around me.
originals.zh: 火焰蔓延，我飘进火海，四周火光闪烁。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 6 段

examples.en: Dry branches blazed in the fireplace.
examples.zh: 干树枝在壁炉中熊熊燃烧。

examples.en: The windows were a blaze of color at sunset.
examples.zh: 日落时，窗户映出一片绚丽色彩。

examples.en: Her research blazed a trail for younger scholars.
examples.zh: 她的研究为年轻学者开辟了道路。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 一把；少数；难对付的人
records.usage: a handful of rice 一把米；a handful of people 少数人；be a handful 让人费心。

originals.text: I thrash and scramble and try to swim back out of it, grabbing handfuls of air and fire, kicking, burning!
originals.zh: 我挂着火苗，拼命挥舞摆动，在空气和火海中手舞足蹈，想游回火海之外！
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 6 段

examples.en: She scattered a handful of seeds on the soil.
examples.zh: 她往土上撒了一把种子。

examples.en: Only a handful of students chose the optional course.
examples.zh: 只有少数学生选了这门选修课。

examples.en: The puppy is a real handful.
examples.zh: 这只小狗真让人费心。

records.meaning: v. 急忙、手脚并用爬起；争抢；打乱；炒蛋

examples.en: She scrambled to her feet when the bell rang.
examples.zh: 铃一响，她就急忙站起来。

examples.en: Passengers scrambled for the last few seats.
examples.zh: 乘客争抢最后几个座位。

examples.en: He scrambled two eggs for breakfast.
examples.zh: 他炒了两个鸡蛋作早餐。

examples.en: The device scrambles the radio signal.
examples.zh: 这个装置会对无线电信号进行扰码。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 猛烈挣扎；痛打；大败
records.usage: thrash about 四处乱扑腾；thrash out a problem 反复讨论解决。

originals.text: I heard scrambling and thrashing near me.
originals.zh: 我听见身旁有人争斗，发出击打和呻吟声。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 92 段

examples.en: The trapped bird thrashed against the net.
examples.zh: 被困的鸟猛烈扑打鸟网。

examples.en: We spent an hour thrashing out the timetable.
examples.zh: 我们花了一小时反复商定时间表。

originals.location: 第 24 章 · 第 111 段

examples.en: The lettering had faded in the sunlight.
examples.zh: 字迹被太阳晒褪色了。

examples.en: The applause faded as the speaker returned.
examples.zh: 发言者回来时，掌声渐渐消失。

records.meaning: v./n. 闪光；眼中一闪的神情
records.usage: glint in the sun 在阳光下闪亮；a glint of amusement 一丝戏谑神色。

originals.text: Stars casting their cool, pale, glinting light.
originals.zh: 星星闪烁着冷酷苍白的光。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 12 段

examples.en: A coin glinted beneath the bench.
examples.zh: 长凳下面有枚硬币闪着光。

examples.en: There was a mischievous glint in her eyes.
examples.zh: 她眼中闪着顽皮的光。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。

records.usage: loom over 赫然耸立于……上方；a crisis looms 危机迫近；weave on a loom 用织布机织布。

originals.text: It was a terrifying, looming, moving wall.
originals.zh: 直到天黑，我们在身后的山坡上只能看见烟雾，仿佛一堵不断逼近的移动之墙，让我们陷入恐惧。
originals.location: 第 24 章 · 第 146 段

examples.en: Flooding loomed as water seeped through the banks and deposited silt across a tract of farmland.
examples.zh: 水渗过河岸，把淤泥沉积在一大片农田上，洪水威胁越来越近。

examples.en: She learned to weave on a wooden loom.
examples.zh: 她学会了用木织机织布。

examples.en: An important deadline is looming.
examples.zh: 一个重要的截止日期正在逼近。

records.meaning: v./n. 蹲伏，蜷身
records.usage: crouch behind 蹲在……后；crouch down 蹲下；常带躲藏或蓄势感。

originals.text: I see it as a crouching animal, perhaps about to spring, more threatening than protective.
originals.zh: 我把它看作一只蹲伏的猛兽，它也许马上就要一跃而起，更像是在发出威胁而不是自我保护。
originals.location: 第 1 章 · 第 14 段

examples.en: The cat crouched beneath the chair.
examples.zh: 猫蹲伏在椅子下面。

examples.en: She crouched down to inspect the tracks.
examples.zh: 她蹲下查看足迹。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: adj. 保护性的；爱护的

examples.zh: 他扭伤脚踝后，一瘸一拐地回了家。

examples.en: The investigation was hobbled by missing records.
examples.zh: 调查因档案缺失而受到阻碍。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 步枪；v. 搜索并翻乱；偷取
records.usage: 名词指枪管内有膛线的一类长枪；rifle through a drawer 翻找抽屉，rifle someone's pockets 翻窃口袋。两种用法须按句法辨认。

originals.text: “Why don’t you buy the rifle for yourself?”
originals.zh: 我没对他笑：“为什么你自己不买？”
originals.location: 第 19 章 · 第 167 段

examples.en: The museum displayed a nineteenth-century rifle.
examples.zh: 博物馆展出了一支十九世纪的步枪。

examples.en: Someone had rifled through the papers on her desk.
examples.zh: 有人把她桌上的文件翻乱了。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 把刀剑等收入鞘；覆盖，包裹
records.usage: sheathe a sword 把剑收鞘；be sheathed in metal/ice 被金属／冰包覆。名词 sheath 没有词尾 e；其复数为 sheaths。

originals.text: Many were armed with sheathed knives, rifles, and, of course, visible, holstered handguns.
originals.zh: 很多人带着收好的刀具、步枪和虽然装在枪套里但是明显可见的手枪。
originals.location: 第 15 章 · 第 101 段

examples.en: The actor sheathed the sword at the end of the scene.
examples.zh: 这场戏结束时，演员把剑收进鞘里。

examples.en: By morning, the branches were sheathed in ice.
examples.zh: 到了早上，树枝都裹上了一层冰。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 大口吞咽；因紧张而吞口水；n. 一大口
records.usage: gulp down a drink 大口喝下；take a gulp of water 喝一大口水。a gulp of air 猛吸一口气；描写紧张时 gulp 可不带宾语。

originals.text: They took quick, furtive gulps, as though they were doing something shameful—or something dangerous.
originals.zh: 走路过程中几乎没有人吃东西，我看见几个人从水壶里喝水，鬼鬼祟祟地猛灌几口，仿佛在做什么丢脸的事—或者说危险的事。
originals.location: 第 15 章 · 第 102 段

examples.en: He took a long gulp of cold water.
examples.zh: 他喝了一大口凉水。

examples.en: She gulped when she saw the size of the audience.
examples.zh: 看到那么多观众，她紧张得咽了一下口水。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n./v. 突然倾斜，踉跄，猛然一沉
records.usage: lurch forward；one's stomach lurches 心里猛地一沉；leave someone in the lurch 撇下不管。

originals.text: The woman sat where she had fallen for a few seconds, then lurched to her feet and began walking again, leaning forward under her huge pack.
originals.zh: 女人在她倒下的地方坐了一会儿，然后摇晃着站起来继续行走，巨大的背包压得她直不起身体。
originals.location: 第 15 章 · 第 103 段

examples.en: The boat lurched sideways in the wave.
examples.zh: 船在浪中猛地向一侧倾斜。

examples.en: My stomach lurched when I saw the empty safe.
examples.zh: 看见空保险箱，我心里猛地一沉。

examples.en: They left us in the lurch just before the deadline.
examples.zh: 他们在截止日期前把我们撇下不管了。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 捕食者；掠夺者；利用他人弱点牟利或施害的人
records.usage: 自然界中与 prey（猎物）相对；与 scavenger（食腐者）侧重点不同。用于人带强烈贬义，强调利用、控制或伤害弱者；形容词 predatory。

originals.text: “Predators will look at a group like the five of us and move on to easier prey.”
originals.zh: 我说，“掠夺者会看一眼我们五人组，然后去寻找更容易的目标。”
originals.location: 第 17 章 · 第 174 段

examples.en: The rabbit froze when it sensed a predator nearby.
examples.zh: 兔子察觉附近有捕食者时僵住了。

examples.en: The investigation exposed financial predators targeting elderly residents.
examples.zh: 调查揭露了一些专门利用老年居民牟利的金融掠夺者。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 具有“共享感受”能力的人（书中用法）；分享者，分担者
records.usage: 普通 sharer 是 share 加 -er；本书赋予它特定意义，指会体验他人痛苦或感受的 hyperempathy 者。不要把小说中的身体反应机制当作现实临床事实。

originals.text: “Some feelers—sharers—can’t have any kids.
originals.zh: 一些感觉拥有者—分享者—无法生孩子
originals.location: 第 24 章 · 第 117 段

examples.en: In this fictional world, a sharer can experience another person's pain.
examples.zh: 在这个虚构世界里，共感者能体验他人的疼痛。

examples.en: The flat-sharers agreed to divide the electricity bill equally.
examples.zh: 合租者同意平摊电费。

records.note: 这是作品中的特定名称、概念或用法；不据此赋予普通 CEFR 等级。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: v. 背叛；泄露；无意显露
records.usage: betray a friend/trust 背叛朋友／辜负信任；betray a secret 泄密。trembling hands betray fear 表示身体反应泄露恐惧，不意味着主动背叛。

originals.text: I might fail you, but if I could help myself, I wouldn’t betray you.”
originals.zh: 我也许会辜负你，但是只要我还活着，就不会背叛你。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 153 段

examples.en: She regained her composure, but a sudden wail betrayed her grief.
examples.zh: 她恢复了镇定，一声突然的哀号却暴露了悲痛。

examples.en: His trembling hands betrayed his nervousness.
examples.zh: 他颤抖的双手暴露了紧张。

examples.en: He felt she had betrayed his trust by publishing the private letters.
examples.zh: 她公开那些私人信件后，他觉得她辜负了自己的信任。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: adj. 不动声色的；面无表情的
records.usage: 来自 poker face，指像打牌时不暴露底牌那样隐藏情绪；不是天生表情少的医学判断。remain poker-faced、a poker-faced reply。

originals.text: And you’re so damned poker-faced most of the time.
originals.zh: 而且大多数时候都一脸严肃……”
originals.location: 第 15 章 · 第 114 段

examples.en: She remained poker-faced while everyone else laughed.
examples.zh: 别人都笑了，她却仍然不动声色。

examples.en: His poker-faced delivery made the joke even funnier.
examples.zh: 他一本正经地讲出笑话，反而显得更好笑。

records.gradeSource: 依据 English Vocabulary Profile 编制的 C2 二手汇编，作词条参考；不是官方穷尽清单。
records.meaning: n. 水疱；鼓包；v. 起疱；猛烈批评
records.usage: a blister on one's heel 脚跟上的水疱；blistered paint 起泡的油漆。blistering criticism 酷烈的批评；blistering heat 酷热，不宜逐字译为起疱。

originals.text: It isn’t only the blisters and sore feet, although we’ve got those.
originals.zh: 虽然我们都起了水泡，感到脚部酸痛，但是不只有这些。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 4 段

examples.en: The long walk left blisters on both heels.
examples.zh: 长途步行让她两个脚跟都起了水疱。

examples.en: Heat had blistered the paint around the window.
examples.zh: 热气使窗边的油漆起了泡。

examples.en: The report contained a blistering criticism of the management.
examples.zh: 报告对管理层作出了尖锐批评。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: n. 果核；坑；v. 使相争；去核
records.usage: a peach pit 桃核，美式常用，英式也说 stone。a deep pit 深坑；pit A against B 使双方对抗，pitted cherries 去核樱桃。

originals.text: Sucking on a plum or apricot pit all day makes you feel less thirsty.
originals.zh: 嘴里整天含着李子核或者杏核，可以缓解口渴。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 5 段

examples.en: She removed the pit from the peach.
examples.zh: 她取出了桃核。

examples.en: A deep pit remained where the tree had stood.
examples.zh: 原来长树的地方留下了一个深坑。

examples.en: The competition pits experienced chefs against talented amateurs.
examples.zh: 这项比赛让经验丰富的厨师与有天赋的业余爱好者展开较量。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 玉米粉；粗磨玉米面
records.usage: 美式 corn 指玉米；cornmeal 常比用于增稠的 cornstarch 粗，二者不能随意等同。常见 cornmeal porridge、cornmeal bread。

originals.text: Soon we’ll run out of it and we’ll have to survive on beans, cornmeal, oats—expensive stuff from stores.
originals.zh: 很快我们就会用光橡子粉，只能依靠豆子、玉米粉和燕麦存活，那些都是从商店买来的贵重食品。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 8 段

examples.en: She stirred the cornmeal slowly into the hot water.
examples.zh: 她把玉米面缓缓搅入热水中。

examples.en: The baker dusted the tray with cornmeal.
examples.zh: 面包师在烤盘上撒了一层玉米粉。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 性能力强的男子（俚语、常物化）；种公畜；耳钉，饰钉；立柱
records.usage: 用来评价男人时可能含性吸引力、自负或种马般的暗示；不宜误作一般“帅哥”。a stud farm 种马场，ear studs 耳钉，wall studs 墙体框架立柱。

originals.text: Three women wanted to know whether two studs like Harry and me didn’t need more than one woman.
originals.zh: 两个女人想知道，我和哈里这样的汉子只有一个女人是不是不够。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 11 段

examples.en: The breeder had unshakable faith in the thoroughbred stallion at his stud farm.
examples.zh: 育种者对种马场里的那匹纯种公马抱有坚定信心。

examples.en: She wore small silver studs in her ears.
examples.zh: 她戴着小小的银耳钉。

examples.en: He liked to present himself as a stud, but his friends found it ridiculous.
examples.zh: 他喜欢把自己塑造成魅力十足、性能力强的男人，朋友们却觉得这很可笑。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 枯萎；干瘪；衰退
records.usage: 植物、果蔬或身体部位可 wither；hopes wither 希望逐渐消失。withering criticism/look 是令人难堪的尖刻批评／眼神，不能总按干枯理解。

originals.text: “Couldn’t I just roast this potato in your coals?” an old man asked, showing us a withered potato.
originals.zh: “我能不能在你们的火坑里烤土豆？”一个老头举着一颗干瘪的土豆问道。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 12 段

originals.text: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away because it lacked moisture.
originals.zh: 有落在磐石上的，一出来就枯干了，因为得不着滋润。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: The potatoes had withered in the warm cupboard.
examples.zh: 土豆在温暖的橱柜里放得干瘪了。

examples.en: Their hopes withered as the weeks passed without news.
examples.zh: 数周过去仍没有消息，他们的希望逐渐消失。

examples.en: She gave him a withering look.
examples.zh: 她用一个锐利而鄙夷的眼神看了他一眼。

examples.en: The seedlings withered in the dry soil.
examples.zh: 幼苗在干土里枯萎了。

examples.en: Their enthusiasm withered after repeated delays.
examples.zh: 一再拖延让他们的热情逐渐消退。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 偏执疑惧；过度猜忌；妄想性的被害感
records.usage: 日常可夸张指疑心很重；临床语境则需更准确判断，不与普通谨慎画等号。paranoia about security 对安全的过度担忧；形容词 paranoid。

originals.text: But we need our paranoia to keep us alive.
originals.zh: 太神经质，可是我们需要偏执来保证生存。该死！
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 13 段

examples.en: The atmosphere of secrecy fed his paranoia.
examples.zh: 保密的氛围助长了他的疑惧。

examples.en: She joked that her paranoia about losing files explained all the backups.
examples.zh: 她开玩笑说，自己如此怕丢文件，所以才做了这么多备份。

records.gradeSource: 依据 English Vocabulary Profile 编制的 C2 二手汇编，作词条参考；不是官方穷尽清单。
records.meaning: n. 冲动；推动力；脉冲
records.usage: on impulse 一时冲动，resist an impulse 克制冲动；an impulse to leave 想离开的冲动。技术或生理语境 a nerve impulse 是神经冲动，不指情绪。

originals.text: I fight against the impulse.
originals.zh: 我们总想信任别人，我抑制冲动，可哈里还没学会。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 13 段

examples.en: She resisted the impulse to interrupt him.
examples.zh: 她忍住了打断他的冲动。

examples.en: I bought the bright red coat on impulse.
examples.zh: 我一时冲动买下了那件鲜红外套。

records.gradeSource: 依据 English Vocabulary Profile 编制的 C2 二手汇编，作词条参考；不是官方穷尽清单。
records.meaning: n. 带子；肩带；v. 用带捆住或固定
records.usage: a shoulder strap 肩带，tighten a strap 收紧带子；strap something to something 将某物捆在另一物上。strapped for cash 是手头拮据，不能按绑住现金理解。

originals.text: While the victim was distracted by the little kid, two bigger kids tripped him, cut his pack straps, dragged the pack off his back, and ran off with it.
originals.zh: 不明智。一个十二三岁的小孩抢到坚果跑掉了，受害者的注意力被小孩吸引的时候，两个更大的孩子绊倒他，割断了他背包的背带，从他背上拽下背包逃走了。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 20 段

examples.en: One strap of the backpack had begun to fray.
examples.zh: 背包的一条肩带开始磨损脱线。

examples.en: They strapped the suitcase to the roof rack.
examples.zh: 他们把箱子捆在车顶行李架上。

examples.en: We are a little strapped for cash this month.
examples.zh: 我们这个月手头有点紧。

records.gradeSource: Oxford 3000／5000 词条级别参考；不等同于核定书中每个具体义项。
records.meaning: v. 干涉；妨碍；产生干扰
records.usage: interfere with 妨碍正常运作；interfere in 干涉他人事务。

originals.text: The whole thing happened so fast that no one could have interfered if they’d wanted to.
originals.zh: 整件事发生得飞快，即使有人想干预也没有时间反应，更何况没人愿意帮忙。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 20 段

examples.en: Street noise interfered with the recording.
examples.zh: 街道噪声干扰了录音。

examples.en: She dislikes people interfering in her private life.
examples.zh: 她不喜欢别人干涉她的私生活。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 擦伤；磨损；磨蚀
records.usage: 皮肤 abrasion 常指表层擦破；与 bruise（皮下淤伤）区别。工业或地理语境指摩擦磨损；abrasion-resistant 耐磨的。

originals.text: The victim was unhurt except for bruises and abrasions—the sort of thing I had to put up with every day back in the neighborhood.
originals.zh: 除了几处—在社区生活时我也总是经受—瘀青和擦伤，受害者没有重伤，可是他的补给没有了。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 20 段

examples.en: The nurse recorded a small abrasion on his elbow.
examples.zh: 护士记录了他肘部的一处小擦伤。

examples.en: The coating protects the surface from abrasion.
examples.zh: 涂层保护表面免受磨损。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: adj. 逞男子气概的；强调强硬阳刚的；n. 大男子气概
records.usage: 常带讽刺或批评，指把强硬、冒险、拒绝示弱等当成男性身份表现；macho image/attitude。不是赞美“勇敢”的中性同义词。

originals.text: He leaned back against a rock, and said with amazement, “You damn sure talk macho enough to be a guy.”
originals.zh: 他向后靠在一块石头上，诧异地说：“你讲起道理来可真像个男人。”
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 32 段

examples.en: He put on a macho voice to hide his nervousness.
examples.zh: 他装出一副硬汉腔调来掩饰紧张。

examples.en: The office's macho culture discouraged people from asking for help.
examples.zh: 办公室逞强的文化让人不敢求助。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: adj. 苍白憔悴的；无力的
records.usage: a wan smile 勉强而虚弱的笑；区别 wane 减弱，二者不能混合还原。

originals.text: Harry gave a wan smile.
originals.zh: 哈里无力地一笑。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 37 段

examples.en: He offered a wan smile after the sleepless night.
examples.zh: 一夜未眠后，他勉强笑了一下。

examples.en: Her face looked wan in the morning light.
examples.zh: 晨光下，她的脸显得苍白憔悴。

examples.en: He gave a wan smile and closed his eyes.
examples.zh: 他勉强笑了一下，闭上眼睛。

records.note: wan“苍白、虚弱”与 wane“减弱”不是同一词；原来误归的 waning 已拆到 wane。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v./n. 轻推，轻碰；温和地促使或提醒
records.usage: nudge someone with an elbow 用肘轻碰某人；nudge someone toward a decision 逐渐促使某人作决定。通常比 shove 轻，不一定真的发生身体接触。

originals.text: I was lost in thought about the two of them when Zahra nudged me with her foot.
originals.zh: 我陷入对他俩的沉思，这时扎赫拉用脚碰了碰我。
originals.location: 第 16 章 · 第 40 段

examples.en: She nudged me gently when my name was called.
examples.zh: 有人叫到我的名字时，她轻轻碰了我一下。

examples.en: A reminder on the screen nudged him to finish the application.
examples.zh: 屏幕上的提醒促使他把申请填完。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: v. 位于两旁；n. 身体侧腹；侧面，侧翼

examples.en: The novel's borderworks offer jobs under harsh conditions.
examples.zh: 小说中的边境工业场所提供工作，但条件恶劣。

examples.en: The characters debate whether the borderworks are a viable destination.
examples.zh: 人物们讨论边境工场是否是可行的去处。

records.meaning: v./n. 小口啃、轻咬；一点兴趣

originals.text: He looked down at Doe who was still nibbling at a piece of sweet potato.

examples.en: The rabbit nibbled at a cabbage leaf.
examples.zh: 兔子小口啃着卷心菜叶。

examples.en: Unexpected fees nibbled away at our savings.
examples.zh: 意外费用一点点蚕食我们的积蓄。

examples.en: We advertised the car but haven't had a nibble.
examples.zh: 我们登了卖车广告，但还没人表示兴趣。

records.meaning: n. 脆弱、易受伤害；弱点、漏洞
records.usage: vulnerability to disease；emotional vulnerability；security vulnerabilities 可数指具体漏洞。

originals.text: He did a lot to keep people away from him—keep them from knowing too much about him, keep them from seeing what he was feeling, or that he was feeling anything—a male sharer, desperate to hide his terrible vulnerability?
originals.zh: 我一直在考虑格雷森，他做了很多事来让别人远离他—防止他们对他了解太多，以免他们看出他的感觉或看出他有感觉—一位拥有超共感的男性，拼命隐藏自己可怕的弱点？
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 67 段

examples.en: The report examines the coast's vulnerability to flooding.
examples.zh: 报告考察了海岸遭受洪灾的风险。

examples.en: The actor allowed a moment of vulnerability to show.
examples.zh: 演员流露出了一瞬脆弱。

examples.en: The update fixes several security vulnerabilities.
examples.zh: 更新修复了几个安全漏洞。

records.meaning: n. 埋葬、葬礼；掩埋

originals.text: At last Bankole has decided that they aren’t going to come, and that it’s time his sister and her family had a decent burial.
originals.zh: 警察一直没来，后来班克尔确定他们不会来，觉得应该给妹妹及其家人举行一场像样的葬礼。

examples.en: The family gathered for the burial.
examples.zh: 家人聚在一起参加下葬仪式。

examples.en: Archaeologists discovered an ancient burial site.
examples.zh: 考古学家发现了一处古代墓葬遗址。

records.meaning: v. 纪念、以活动或物件缅怀
records.usage: commemorate a person/event；不直接用 commemorate someone to do；名词 commemoration。

originals.text: “Trees are better than stone—life commemorating life.”

originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 80 段

originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 98 段

examples.zh: 尽管发生了争执，合作关系仍然可以挽回。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 面包屑、碎屑；少许

originals.text: Or maybe we’ll just break up into a lot of little states quarreling and fighting with each other over whatever crumbs are left.
originals.zh: “不。”他把我拉到身旁用一只手搂住我，“人类肯定会幸存，其他一些国家也会，也许它们会吞并我国的余部，也许我们会分裂成各州，相互为了点残羹冷炙争吵打斗。如今各州相互封闭，把州界当作国境线，几乎就形成了那种局面。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 100 段

examples.en: She brushed the crumbs off her sleeve.
examples.zh: 她掸掉了袖子上的面包屑。

examples.en: The apology offered him a small crumb of comfort.
examples.zh: 那句道歉让他得到了一点安慰。

records.meaning: adj. 毛发蓬乱且长的
records.usage: a shaggy dog/beard；a shaggy-dog story 为冗长、结尾无趣的故事，可作为固定表达另识别。

originals.text: He shook his shaggy head, his hair, beard, and serious expression making him look more than a little like an old picture I used to have of Frederick Douglass.
originals.zh: 他摇摇毛发旺盛的脑袋，头发、胡子和严肃的表情让他看起来非常像我以前的一张老照片上的弗雷德里克·道格拉斯。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 106 段

examples.en: A shaggy pony stood by the gate.
examples.zh: 一匹长毛蓬乱的小马站在门边。

examples.en: His shaggy hair fell over his eyes.
examples.zh: 他蓬乱的长发垂下来遮住了眼睛。

records.meaning: v. 吞食、狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地阅读；吞噬

originals.text: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
originals.zh: 有一个撒种的出去撒种。撒的时候，有落在路旁的，被人践踏，天上的飞鸟又来吃尽了。

examples.en: The birds devoured the scattered seeds.
examples.zh: 鸟儿吃光了撒落的种子。

examples.en: She devoured the novel in one evening.
examples.zh: 她一晚上就如饥似渴地读完了小说。

examples.en: The flames devoured the wooden shed.
examples.zh: 火焰吞噬了木棚。

records.meaning: v. 播种；散播、引发；n. 母猪
records.usage: 动词 sow–sowed–sown/sowed；sow seeds/doubt；动词读音与 so 相同，母猪义与 now 押韵。

originals.text: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
originals.zh: 有一个撒种的出去撒种。撒的时候，有落在路旁的，被人践踏，天上的飞鸟又来吃尽了。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: We sowed the beans in early spring.
examples.zh: 我们在早春播下豆子。

examples.en: The misleading article sowed doubt about the results.
examples.zh: 误导性文章使人们对结果产生怀疑。

examples.en: The sow rested beside her piglets.
examples.zh: 母猪躺在小猪旁休息。

records.meaning: n. 播种者；传播者

originals.text: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
originals.zh: 有一个撒种的出去撒种。撒的时候，有落在路旁的，被人践踏，天上的飞鸟又来吃尽了。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: The painting shows a sower crossing a field.
examples.zh: 画中是一位穿过田地的播种者。

examples.en: The essay describes the teacher as a sower of ideas.
examples.zh: 文章把教师描写为思想的播种者。

records.meaning: v. 踩踏、行走；n. 轮胎花纹、步态
records.usage: tread–trod–trodden/trod；tread down 踩平；tread carefully 谨慎行事；tread water 踩水或毫无进展。

originals.text: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
originals.zh: 有一个撒种的出去撒种。撒的时候，有落在路旁的，被人践踏，天上的飞鸟又来吃尽了。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: The seedlings had been trodden down.

examples.zh: 谈判期间我们必须谨慎行事。

examples.en: The tyres had almost no tread left.
examples.zh: 轮胎上的花纹几乎磨光了。

records.meaning: n. 水分、湿气
records.usage: retain/absorb moisture；不可数；moist 潮润的，与完全浸湿 wet 程度不同。

originals.text: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away because it lacked moisture.
originals.zh: 有落在磐石上的，一出来就枯干了，因为得不着滋润。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.zh: 盖子把水分留在容器内。

examples.en: Moisture had damaged the photographs.
examples.zh: 湿气损坏了照片。

records.gradeSource: 按阅读语境补入；未逐义项核定 CEFR，不表示一定高于 C2。
records.meaning: n. 荆棘刺；棘手的人或事

originals.text: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
originals.zh: 有落在荆棘里的，荆棘一同生长，把它挤住了。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: A thorn caught in the sleeve of my coat.
examples.zh: 一根刺钩住了我的外套袖子。

examples.en: The unresolved dispute remains a thorn in the mayor's side.
examples.zh: 悬而未决的争议仍是市长的心头刺。

records.usage: increase hundredfold；a hundredfold return；-fold 表倍数，在圣经或文学中可写极丰厚收获。

originals.text: And others fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bore fruit an hundredfold.
originals.zh: 又有落在好土里的，生长起来，结实百倍。
originals.location: 第 25 章 · 第 112 段

examples.en: The investment produced a hundredfold return over several decades.
examples.zh: 这项投资在数十年间带来了百倍回报。

examples.en: The seed yielded a hundredfold in the parable.
examples.zh: 在比喻中，种子结出了百倍的收成。
